text: The relation between time t and distance x for a moving body is given as $t = mx^{2} + nx$, where m and n are constants. The retardation of the motion is : (When v stands for velocity)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Differentiating $t=mx^{2}+nx$ with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dt}{dx}=2mx+n\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{2mx+n}$

The acceleration is

$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=v\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2mx+n}\left (-\dfrac{2m}{(2mx+n)^{2}}\right )=-\dfrac{2m}{(2mx+n)^{3}}=-2mv^{3}$

The negative sign shows that the body is slowing down, so the retardation (magnitude of the deceleration) is $2mv^{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: The instantaneous velocity of a particle moving in a straight line is given as $V=αt+βt^{2}$, where $α$ and $β$ are constants. The distance travelled by the particle between 1s and 2s is :

solution.body:
$V=αt+βt^{2}$

$\frac{ds}{dt}=αt+βt^{2}$

$\int\limits _{S_{1}}^{S_{2}}ds=\int\limits _{1}^{2}(αt+βt^{2})dt$

$S_{2}-S_{1}=\left [\frac{αt^{2}}{2}+\frac{βt^{3}}{3}\right ]_{1}^{2}$

As particle is not changing direction 

So distance = displacement

$=\frac{3α}{2}+\frac{7β}{3}$

text: When radiation of wavelength $λ$ is incident on a metallic surface, the stopping potential of ejected photoelectrons is 4.8 V. If the same surface is illuminated by radiation of double the previous wavelength, then the stopping potential becomes 1.6 V. The threshold wavelength of the metal is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$V_{s}=hv-𝜙$

$4.8=\frac{hc}{λ}-𝜙$ ..... (i)

$1.6=\frac{hc}{2λ}-𝜙$ ..... (ii)

Using above equation (i) - (ii)

$3.2=\frac{hc}{λ}-\frac{hc}{2λ}$

$3.2=\frac{hc}{2λ}$ ..... (iii)

$\left [λ=\frac{hc}{6.4}\right ]$

Put in equation (ii)

$𝜙$ = 1.6

$\frac{hc}{λ_{th}}=1.6$

$λ_{th}=\frac{hc}{1.6}$

$=\left (\frac{hc}{6.4}\right )\times 4=4λ$

text: Two vectors $\vec{X}$ and $\vec{Y}$ have equal magnitude. The magnitude of ($\vec{X}$ $-$ $\vec{Y}$) is n times the magnitude of ($\vec{X}$ + $\vec{Y}$). The angle between $\vec{X}$ and $\vec{Y}$ is :

solution.body:
Given X = Y

$=n\sqrt{X^{2}+Y^{2}+2XY\cos θ}$

Square both sides

$2X^{2}(1-\cos θ)=n^{2}.2X^{2}(1+\cos θ)$

$1-\cos θ=n^{2}+n^{2}\cos θ$

$\cos θ=\frac{1-n^{2}}{1+n^{2}}$

$θ=\cos ^{-1}\left [\frac{n^{2}-1}{-n^{2}-1}\right ]$

text:
A light beam of wavelength 500 nm is incident on a metal having work function of 1.25 eV, placed in a magnetic field of intensity B. The electrons emitted perpendicular to the magnetic field B, with maximum kinetic energy are bent into circular arc of radius 30 cm. The value of B is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-7} T$.

 Given hc = 20 $\times$ $10^{-26} J-m$, mass of electron = 9 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Photon energy: $E=\dfrac{hc}{λ}=\dfrac{20\times 10^{-26}}{500\times 10^{-9}}=4\times 10^{-19}\text{J}=2.5\text{eV}$.

Maximum kinetic energy: $K_{\max }=2.5-1.25=1.25\text{eV}=1.25\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}=2\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$.

Momentum: $p=\sqrt{2mK_{\max }}=\sqrt{2\times 9\times 10^{-31}\times 2\times 10^{-19}}=6\times 10^{-25}\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.

For motion perpendicular to the field, $r=\dfrac{p}{eB}$, so

$B=\dfrac{p}{er}=\dfrac{6\times 10^{-25}}{1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 0.30}=1.25\times 10^{-5}\text{T}=125\times 10^{-7}\text{T}$

Hence, the answer is 125.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift
